title: Access Governor: evaluation engine + runtime admission interceptor for multi-surface RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Build a performant, auditable policy evaluation engine ("Access Governor") plus a lightweight runtime admission interceptor that enforces RBAC v2 across API, runtime (serving requests), and Console surfaces. This ticket covers the core evaluator, an interceptor library for runtimes and API gateways, admin control hooks for the Console, and the audit emission contract. Goal: provide consistent allow/deny/permit-with-conditions decisions with sub-10ms median evaluation for hot paths and streaming audit events to our audit-pipeline.

Key design goals: consistent semantics across surfaces, low tail-latency, compact telemetry, ability to evaluate scoped conditions (resource attributes, token metadata, request route, tenant flags), and safe fallback behaviors during rollout. Must integrate with SSO/SAML identity attributes and Dedicated/Private deployments (local policy bundles + central control plane).
acceptance_criteria: Evaluation engine produces canonical decision payload (allow/deny/warn) with reason and rule_id
Interceptor rejects unauthorized calls at API gateway and serving runtime with <50ms 99th percentile under standard load
Audit events emitted for all decisions (allow and deny) in newline-delimited JSON schema and reach audit-pipeline staging
Console admin workflows can create, preview, and roll out policies to targeted environments with role scoping
Migration path documented from RBACv1: mapping tool + compatibility shim for legacy ACLs
Automated test harness with 2000 synthetic policy permutations and performance regression alerts
technical_notes: Core evaluator is a lightweight WASM runtime that consumes compiled policies (policy IR) to avoid language dependencies
Policy language derived from our RFC: expressions, scopes, resource-typed attributes, time windows, and delegation rules
Evaluator includes a small LRU cache keyed by (principal, resource-type, action, token-version) to accelerate repeated checks
Interceptor should expose a gRPC/HTTP v2 interface and a tiny sidecar library for in-process enforcement for on-prem deployments
Audit payload spec: timestamp, decision, principal_id, principal_attrs, resource, action, rule_id, policy_version, request_id, trace_id, locality
SSO/SAML: evaluator accepts enriched identity attributes from IdP mapping layer; attribute mappings configurable per-tenant
Fallback behavior: when policy store unreachable -> use last-known-good policies for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses 'deny-open' with alerting by default for P0 routes
Metrics: decision_latency_histogram, cache_hit_ratio, policy_compile_errors, enforcement_failures, audit_emit_failures
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype evaluator as WASM module and validate with 500 synthetic policies (Spike) - owner: Diego
2) Define canonical decision schema and audit event contract - owner: Security Eng
3) Implement HTTP/gRPC interceptor shim and local sidecar adapter - owner: Runtime Team
4) Integrate SSO/SAML attribute enrichment and attribute-based checks - owner: Identity Team
5) Add Console admin hooks: policy authoring preview, canary targeting, and rollout controls - owner: Console PM
6) Build migration wizard for RBAC v1 -> v2 mappings and a compatibility mode for 30 days - owner: PM
7) Load test under synthetic traffic and tune cache/kernels - owner: Perf Eng
8) Security review, pen-test, and staged rollout to internal, staging, then production - owner: Security
9) Post-rollout: monitor telemetry, ship regression alerts, and complete runbook - owner: SRE
risks: Policy explosion: large tenant policies may cause compilation churn and memory blowups
Latency regression on tail under heavy multi-tenant concurrency if cache invalidation not tuned
Inconsistent identity attributes from SSO mappings across IdPs causing access gaps
Audit pipeline backpressure could lead to dropped events unless backpressure or buffering handled
Migration complexity: incorrect mapping may temporarily expand privileges; requires conservative defaults
qa_plan: Unit tests for evaluator semantics (expression coverage > 95%)
End-to-end test matrix across API, runtime, console with both hosted and Dedicated configs
Performance benchmarks: baseline, 10x load, and long-tail latencies measured; regression gates
Chaos test: simulate policy-store outages and verify fallback behaviors and alerts
Penetration test focused on bypass vectors and identity spoofing scenarios
